items.q: Figures released by the grid operator on Monday comprehensively ______ the allegation that the country had been days away from rolling blackouts.
items.vi: Số liệu do đơn vị vận hành lưới điện công bố hôm thứ Hai đã bác bỏ hoàn toàn cáo buộc rằng đất nước chỉ còn vài ngày nữa là phải cắt điện luân phiên.
items.explanation: Refute = prove a claim false, and it takes a direct object: refuted the allegation. ✗ argued — you argue a case or argue that something is true; you cannot 'argue an allegation'; ✗ objected — needs to (object to a plan) and means protest, not disprove; ✗ disagreed — needs with and gives an opinion, not proof from figures.

items.q: The sponsor's late withdrawal threw ______ just weeks before the new stadium was due to open.
items.vi: Việc nhà tài trợ rút lui vào phút chót đã phá hỏng kế hoạch chỉ vài tuần trước ngày sân vận động mới dự kiến khai trương.
items.explanation: Throw a spanner in the works = suddenly wreck a plan; the clues are the verb threw and the stadium opening that is now at risk. ✗ a fly in the ointment — a small thing that spoils something; it is one, never thrown; ✗ a bone of contention — a subject people keep arguing over; ✗ a nail in the coffin — one more step towards failure; you put a nail in the coffin, not throw it.

items.q: ______ had the vaccine trial's results been published when three rival laboratories announced they were abandoning their own programmes.
items.vi: Kết quả thử nghiệm vắc-xin vừa mới được công bố thì ba phòng thí nghiệm đối thủ đã tuyên bố từ bỏ chương trình của riêng họ.
items.explanation: Hardly … when: the clue is when after the inverted past perfect (had … been published when). ✗ No sooner — pairs with than, not with when; ✗ Not only — pairs with but (also) and adds a second point, not a time sequence; ✗ Seldom — means 'rarely' and forms no pair with when at all.

items.q: Rolling blackouts ______ a serious threat to the region's hospitals, which cannot run their ventilators on generators for long.
items.vi: Cắt điện luân phiên gây ra mối đe dọa nghiêm trọng cho các bệnh viện trong vùng, vốn không thể chạy máy thở bằng máy phát điện lâu được.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is pose a threat (present a danger); the clue is the noun threat with a situation as subject. ✗ make — you make a threat only when a person threatens someone in words; blackouts cannot; ✗ do — never combines with threat; ✗ put — collocates with at risk (put hospitals at risk), not with threat.

items.q: Despite weeks of pressure from broadcasters, the league refused to ______ and kept every kick-off time unchanged.
items.vi: Dù bị các đài truyền hình gây sức ép suốt nhiều tuần, giải đấu vẫn không chịu nhượng bộ và giữ nguyên mọi giờ thi đấu.
items.explanation: Give in = yield to pressure, and it needs no object; the clues are refused to and kept … unchanged. ✗ give off — emit heat or a smell, and needs an object; ✗ give out — distribute (needs an object) or, on its own, stop working / run out — not yielding; ✗ give away — reveal a secret or donate, and needs an object.

items.q: The press commission recommended that the broadcaster ______ its correction on the front page of its website rather than bury it in a footnote.
items.vi: Ủy ban báo chí khuyến nghị đài truyền hình đăng bản đính chính lên trang đầu của trang web thay vì giấu nó trong một ghi chú cuối trang.
items.explanation: After recommend that the verb takes the bare subjunctive: that the broadcaster print; the clue is recommended that. ✗ prints — the ordinary present with -s; a subjunctive verb never agrees with its subject; ✗ printed — past tense, but the recommendation is about a future action; ✗ would print — a conditional, not used after verbs of demand, suggestion or recommendation.

items.q: Once the replay had been shown on the big screen, the coach was forced to ______ that the goal had been perfectly legitimate.
items.vi: Khi đoạn quay chậm được chiếu lên màn hình lớn, huấn luyện viên buộc phải thừa nhận rằng bàn thắng hoàn toàn hợp lệ.
items.explanation: Concede that = reluctantly admit something is true; the clues are was forced to and the that-clause. ✗ consent — agree to a request, takes to + noun or infinitive, never that; ✗ comply — obey a rule, takes with; ✗ conform — follow accepted standards, takes to / with; none of the three can report a fact.

items.q: Aware that the drivers' union was losing patience, the ministry ______ by promising a review of shift patterns before the end of the year.
items.vi: Biết công đoàn tài xế đang mất kiên nhẫn, bộ đã nhượng bộ chút ít bằng cách hứa xem xét lại lịch ca làm việc trước cuối năm.
items.explanation: Throw someone a bone = give a small concession to keep them quiet; the clue is the modest promise of 'a review' to a union that is losing patience. ✗ threw in the towel — gave up completely, but the ministry did not surrender; ✗ threw its weight around — used its power to bully, the opposite of a soft promise; ✗ threw caution to the wind — acted recklessly, which a careful promise is not.

items.q: Judging by the vibration recorded within an hour of start-up, the turbine ______ been installed correctly.
items.vi: Căn cứ vào độ rung ghi nhận được chỉ trong vòng một giờ sau khi khởi động, tua-bin chắc chắn đã không được lắp đặt đúng cách.
items.explanation: Judging by introduces a deduction, and the vibration is evidence that correct installation was impossible: can't have been (negative deduction about the past). ✗ must have — deduces the opposite, that it certainly was installed correctly; ✗ needn't have — says a past action was unnecessary, not a deduction; ✗ should have — criticises a past failure; the evidence here shows what is true, not what was advisable.

items.q: Having sat on the ______ for months, the regulator finally came ______ in favour of a single national grid operator.
items.vi: Sau nhiều tháng lưỡng lự không chọn bên nào, cơ quan quản lý cuối cùng đã quyết định ủng hộ mô hình một đơn vị vận hành lưới điện quốc gia duy nhất.
items.explanation: Sit on the fence = refuse to take sides, and come down in favour of = finally decide for; the clues are for months then finally. ✗ wall / down — 'sit on the wall' is not an idiom; ✗ fence / up — 'come up in favour of' does not exist; come up = arise; ✗ line / out — 'sit on the line' means nothing (come out in favour of alone would be fine).

items.q: ______ the home side dominated possession for eighty minutes, it was the visitors who created the clearer chances.
items.vi: Mặc dù đội chủ nhà kiểm soát bóng áp đảo suốt tám mươi phút, chính đội khách mới là bên tạo ra những cơ hội rõ rệt hơn.
items.explanation: Although is a conjunction, and the blank is followed by a full clause (the home side dominated) that must be joined to the main clause. ✗ Despite — a preposition: takes a noun or -ing (despite dominating), not a clause; ✗ However — an adverb; it needs a full stop or semicolon before the second sentence; ✗ Nevertheless — also an adverb, so it cannot link two clauses in one sentence.

items.q: The columnist stopped short of an outright accusation, merely ______ that the sprinter's sudden improvement owed more to chemistry than to training.
items.vi: Cây bút bình luận không đưa ra lời buộc tội thẳng thừng mà chỉ ám chỉ rằng sự tiến bộ đột ngột của vận động viên chạy nước rút là nhờ hóa chất nhiều hơn là nhờ tập luyện.
items.explanation: Insinuate = suggest something unpleasant indirectly; the clues are stopped short of an outright accusation and merely. ✗ proclaiming — declaring openly and loudly, not hinting; ✗ pronouncing — declaring formally or officially (pronounce a verdict); ✗ announcing — making news publicly known; all three are open statements, the opposite of a hint.

items.q: The pipeline has been running at ______ capacity since the faulty compressor was replaced in March.
items.vi: Đường ống đã vận hành hết công suất kể từ khi máy nén bị lỗi được thay thế hồi tháng Ba.
items.explanation: The collocation is at full capacity (producing the maximum possible); the clue is running at … capacity. ✗ whole — describes a complete object (the whole pipeline), not a level of output; ✗ entire — the same, before countable nouns (the entire route); ✗ complete — finished or lacking nothing (a complete set); none pairs with capacity.

items.q: ______ its survey of the reef, the research vessel headed north to sample a second stretch of coastline before the monsoon arrived.
items.vi: Sau khi hoàn tất khảo sát rạn san hô, tàu nghiên cứu đi lên phía bắc để lấy mẫu ở một dải bờ biển thứ hai trước khi gió mùa tới.
items.explanation: The vessel finished the survey before it headed north, and the vessel is the doer, so the perfect active participle Having finished marks the earlier action. ✗ Finished — a past participle here is passive: it would mean the vessel itself was finished; ✗ Being finished — also passive, and being gives no 'earlier action' sense; ✗ To have finished — an infinitive expresses purpose or result, not what happened first.

items.q: The night editor asked the reporter at the mine to ______ as the rescue unfolded, even if it meant calling at three in the morning.
items.vi: Biên tập viên ca đêm yêu cầu phóng viên tại hiện trường mỏ liên tục cập nhật tình hình khi cuộc giải cứu diễn ra, kể cả phải gọi lúc ba giờ sáng.
items.explanation: Keep someone posted = keep sending them the latest news; the clues are as the rescue unfolded and calling at three in the morning. ✗ keep her at bay — hold an enemy or problem away; ✗ keep her in the dark — tell her nothing, the exact opposite; ✗ keep her at arm's length — avoid becoming close to someone.

items.q: ______ the goalkeeper's save in stoppage time, the club would have been relegated on the final day of the season.
items.vi: Nếu không nhờ pha cứu thua của thủ môn ở phút bù giờ, câu lạc bộ đã xuống hạng ngay ngày thi đấu cuối cùng của mùa giải.
items.explanation: The inverted third conditional is Had it not been for (= If it had not been for); the clue is would have been relegated. ✗ Had not it been for — in inversion not follows the subject (had it not), never the auxiliary; ✗ If it had not for — with if you need the full verb: had not been; ✗ Were it not been for — were (second conditional) cannot combine with been; it would be were it not for.

items.q: Under threat of legal action, the newspaper agreed to ______ the story and print an apology in the following day's edition.
items.vi: Trước nguy cơ bị kiện, tờ báo đồng ý rút lại bài viết và đăng lời xin lỗi trong số báo ngày hôm sau.
items.explanation: Retract = withdraw a statement as untrue; the clues are the story and print an apology. ✗ rescind — cancel an order, decision or contract; ✗ revoke — officially take back a licence, permit or right; ✗ repeal — abolish a law; none of these three is used with a news story.

items.q: The club's owners would rather ______ a season in the second tier than sell the stadium to property developers.
items.vi: Các ông chủ câu lạc bộ thà chịu đựng một mùa giải ở hạng hai còn hơn bán sân vận động cho các nhà phát triển bất động sản.
items.explanation: Would rather + bare infinitive when the subject stays the same: would rather endure … than sell; the clue is the bare sell after than, which the blank must match. ✗ to endure — no to after would rather; ✗ enduring — -ing follows prefer, not would rather; ✗ endured — the past form is used only with a different subject (I'd rather they endured).

items.q: Repairs to the transmission line were ______ for a month by a dispute over access to farmland along the route.
items.vi: Việc sửa chữa đường dây truyền tải bị trì hoãn suốt một tháng vì tranh chấp về quyền đi qua đất nông nghiệp dọc tuyến.
items.explanation: Hold up = delay; it is transitive, so it works in the passive were held up for a month by. ✗ held out — resist or last (the supplies held out), intransitive, so no passive; ✗ held on — wait or grip tightly, also intransitive; ✗ set up — establish or arrange; repairs are not 'established' by a dispute.

items.q: It's high time the federation ______ the anti-doping rules it wrote more than a decade ago.
items.vi: Đã đến lúc liên đoàn phải sửa đổi các quy định chống doping mà họ soạn ra từ hơn một thập kỷ trước.
items.explanation: It's high time + past subjunctive: It's high time the federation revised; the past form refers to the present or future and stresses that it should already have happened. ✗ revise — the bare subjunctive follows recommend / suggest that, not it's time; ✗ revises — the present simple is not used after it's (high) time; ✗ has revised — the present perfect would say it has already happened, contradicting the complaint.

items.q: Missing the cup final through injury proved ______: the striker returned fully rested for the World Cup qualifiers.
items.vi: Việc lỡ trận chung kết cúp vì chấn thương hóa ra lại là trong cái rủi có cái may: tiền đạo trở lại với thể trạng sung sức cho vòng loại World Cup.
items.explanation: A blessing in disguise = something that seems bad but turns out well; the clue is proved plus the colon: missing the final led to a well-rested return. ✗ a shot in the dark — a wild guess; ✗ a drop in the ocean — an amount too small to matter; ✗ a storm in a teacup — a big fuss about something unimportant.

items.q: Only ______ of the stadium's eighty thousand seats were empty when the final kicked off.
items.vi: Chỉ có một vài chỗ trong số tám mươi nghìn ghế của sân vận động là còn trống khi trận chung kết bắt đầu.
items.explanation: Seats is plural countable, and only a few = a small number; only already carries the 'not many' meaning, so the positive a few is used. ✗ few — already means 'hardly any' (negative), so only few is not standard English; ✗ a little — used with uncountable nouns (a little water); ✗ little — uncountable and negative, so wrong twice.

items.q: The inquiry's report drew a ______ distinction between honest reporting and the paid content that had been dressed up as news.
items.vi: Báo cáo của cuộc điều tra phân biệt rõ ràng giữa đưa tin trung thực và nội dung được trả tiền nhưng được khoác vỏ tin tức.
items.explanation: The collocation is draw a sharp distinction (= a very clear one); the clue is distinction between. ✗ strong — collocates with argument / case / evidence; the standard adjectives for a distinction are sharp, clear or fine; ✗ hard — describes a difficult decision or a hard line, not a distinction; ✗ heavy — collocates with rain / traffic / losses.

items.q: Two independent engineers have since ______ the whistleblower's account of cracks in the dam's spillway.
items.vi: Hai kỹ sư độc lập sau đó đã xác nhận lời kể của người tố giác về các vết nứt ở đập tràn của con đập.
items.explanation: Corroborate = confirm an account with further evidence, and it takes a direct object: corroborated the whistleblower's account. ✗ cooperated — work together, needs with; ✗ coincided — happen at the same time or agree by chance, needs with and cannot take an account as its object; ✗ conformed — follow rules or standards, needs to / with.

items.q: Once the last sticking points over image rights had been ______, the broadcasting deal was ______ by both boards on Monday.
items.vi: Khi những vướng mắc cuối cùng về bản quyền hình ảnh đã được giải quyết, thỏa thuận phát sóng được cả hai hội đồng quản trị phê duyệt hôm thứ Hai.
items.explanation: Iron out = resolve small problems (the sticking points), and sign off = formally approve (by both boards). ✗ ironed off / sealed off — 'iron off' does not exist, and seal off = close an area; ✗ wiped out / signed off — wipe out = destroy completely, too violent for settling disagreements; ✗ ironed out / sent off — send off = order a player off the pitch or post a letter, not approve a deal.
